YOUR NOBLETON

How much down payment do you need?

Understand the minimum, the insurance and the cash you still need at closing.

Prepared by Nobleton.ca editorial team · Suggest a correction

On this page

  • Minimum down payment
  • Mortgage default insurance
  • Keep room for closing and everyday life
  • More about life in Nobleton

Minimum down payment

For an eligible insured purchase below $1.5 million, the minimum is 5% of the first $500,000 plus 10% of the amount above $500,000. A purchase of $1.5 million or more requires at least 20% down. Lenders may require more based on the property and your circumstances.

Mortgage default insurance

With less than 20% down, an eligible purchase generally needs mortgage default insurance. It protects the lender, not the borrower. The premium can usually be added to the loan; Ontario’s 8% tax on the premium must be paid separately. Our calculator estimates these amounts using CMHC’s published standard premiums.

Keep room for closing and everyday life

Your down payment is only part of the cash required. Ask your lawyer and mortgage professional to estimate land transfer tax, legal costs, adjustments and any other applicable expenses. Leave room for maintenance, utilities and an emergency reserve.

General information, not personalized financial or legal advice. Eligibility and actual terms depend on the lender, insurer and property. Reviewed November 9, 2026.
